newsitem.title: USA: W.House's Hilley upbeat on finishing budget pact.
newsitem.headline: W.House's Hilley upbeat on finishing budget pact.

text.p: White House Legislative Director John Hilley said Monday he was optimistic that the outline of the 2002 balanced budget agreement, announced at the beginning of the month, could be finalized shortly.

"We are moving along very, very well," Hilley told Reuters Financial Television. "In fact I anticipate we will be able to conclude the agreement in all of its details necessary for the budget resolution in the next 24 hours."
Hilley also said President Clinton's $35 billion in scholarships and a higher education tax deduction would be part of the tax bill. "We'll be able to lock that in," he said.
Hilley also said he anticipated the House and Senate budget committtees completing their work toward the end of the week with the budget resolution moving to the floor of each house next week.
"So I think we are on schedule and hopefully we will have the budget resolution passed in both bodies before the (May 26) Memorial Day recess," he said.
